subject: Benchmark: Latency & Throughput acceptance for Aperture Finance - coordination and results
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lam <susan.lam@aperturefinance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark kickoff and acceptance criteria (Aperture)

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the sync earlier. Per our runbook, I’m kicking off the formal benchmarking window so we can validate the latency and throughput targets before we flip traffic to production. Attached: the load_test_config we plan to run and a starter results template.

Quick summary of what Redwood will measure this week:
- Steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) across the settled model variant
- p50/p95/p99 response latency measured server-side (end-to-end include network)
- Tail behaviour under concurrent burst (10s–60s blades)
- Error rate / rate-limiter behavior under sustained concurrency

What we need from you:
1) Confirm the acceptance thresholds below (or propose adjustments):
   - p95 generation latency <= 220 ms (for 128-token average requests)
   - p99 latency <= 450 ms
   - Sustained throughput >= 12,000 tokens/sec (cluster-level)
   - Error rate < 0.5% over 15m windows
2) Provide a representative sample of typical prompt mixes (3–5 templates) — Arjun if you can drop those here that’d be ideal.
3) Approve the test window: Wed 07/31 08:00–12:00 PDT (we will run two 45m steady-state passes and two burst passes).

Plan to publish consolidated results in the Drive folder and send a short summary to your procurement/ops contact.

Attachments: load_test_config.yaml (staging harness), results_template.csv

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415‑555‑0126
Redwood Inference

From: Susan Lam <susan.lam@aperturefinance.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Benchmark kickoff and acceptance criteria (Aperture)

Hi Monica —

Thanks — this looks good. Confirming thresholds look reasonable for our needs. A few clarifications:
- p95 <= 220 ms is acceptable; p99 <= 450 ms is preferred but we can tolerate spikes to ~500 ms during short bursts.
- Throughput target: our end goal is 15k tokens/sec but we are comfortable with 12k for initial go/no-go.
- Error rate: <0.5% is fine, please flag any 4xx/5xx with stack traces.

Arjun (cc’d) will drop a small set of prompt templates by end of day. Wed 07/31 08:00–12:00 PDT works on our side — please use the staging API key you have for Aperture (staging-{redacted}).

Also: can you include a short section in the results doc with recommended config tweaks (batch size, prefix cache enablement) so we can collect internal signoff?

Best,
Susan Lam
Head of Platform Integrations, Aperture Finance
susan.lam@aperturefinance.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Lam <susan.lam@aperturefinance.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@aperturefinance.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 14:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Benchmark kickoff and acceptance criteria (Aperture) — test plan details

Following up with the engineering test plan and expected artifacts. I’ll run the two steady-state passes and two burst passes Monica mentioned — details below.

Test harness summary:
- Runner: k6 + Redwood staging harness (scripts in load_test_config.yaml)
- Model variant: gptx-3.2-q4f16-ml (quantized) pinned for the run to remove variance
- Clients: 8 parallel load generators from two regions (us-west-2 + us-east-1) to approximate real network spread
- Payload mix: 60% short (avg 32 tokens), 30% medium (128 tokens), 10% long (512 tokens)
- Concurrency shape: ramp 0->400 virtual users over 5m; hold for 45m; burst: sudden +60% for 60s then back to baseline
- Instrumentation: per-request server-side timestamping, GPU utilization telemetry, per-host error logs (s3://redwood-bench/aperture/2028-07-31/)

Acceptance/analysis notes:
- We will compute token/sec from server token emission logs and cross-check with client tokens generated to catch dropped responses.
- Tail latency windows will be looked at on 1m and 5m slices; any sustained p99 > 600 ms triggers an incident for investigation (latency_blip tag).

Attachments included: load_test_config.yaml (script), smoke_check.sh (small client-side script).

Operational asks for Aperture:
- Please ensure there are no active canary deployments or other heavy jobs on the staging cluster during the window.
- If you can keep a Slack channel open (#aperture-bench) we’ll post live summaries.

I’ll start the first steady-state pass at 08:05 PDT Wed.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lam <susan.lam@aperturefinance.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@aperturefinance.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Jul 2028 21:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Benchmark kickoff and acceptance criteria (Aperture) — results and recommended next steps

Hi Susan / Arjun —

Thanks for the collaboration today. Quick recap and attached artifacts. Full folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qX-aperture-bench-2028

Summary of runs (two steady passes + two bursts):
- Steady pass A (08:05–08:50 PDT): sustained cluster throughput = 12,450 tokens/sec; p95 = 198 ms; p99 = 392 ms; error rate = 0.14%
- Steady pass B (09:30–10:15 PDT): sustained cluster throughput = 12,880 tokens/sec; p95 = 205 ms; p99 = 410 ms; error rate = 0.12%
- Burst pass 1 (10:30): short 60s spike — p95 240 ms (within acceptable window), p99 520 ms (spike noted); transient scheduler-induced retries accounted for the spike
- Burst pass 2 (11:15): repeat spike — p95 228 ms; p99 465 ms; error rate during burst 0.9% (we saw transient 429s tied to client concurrency window)

Conclusion:
- Outcome: Acceptable for initial production ramp with one operational caveat — burst p99 occasionally exceeds the preferred 450 ms bound.
- Recommendation: enable prefix/KV cache and increase per-worker batch cap from 8 -> 12 for production traffic to reduce burst tail; this is expected to reduce p99 by ~80–120 ms based on our microbenchmarks.

Artifacts attached: aperture_benchmark_results_v1.csv (per-request metrics rollup), aperture_acceptance_summary.pdf (one-page exec summary), load_test_config.yaml (test harness). We’ve also uploaded raw logs to s3://redwood-bench/aperture/2028-07-31/ (access granted to your Aperture staging role).

Next steps / owners:
- Aperture: review and sign acceptance by EOD Fri (Arjun / Susan) — if signed we’ll schedule prod ramp (CS/SE handoff).
- Redwood (Marcus): implement recommended cache + batch config in a canary variant and run two smoke passes.
- Redwood (Monica): prepare the acceptance signoff doc for procurement and create the HubSpot milestone (HS-10923847).

If you want, we can walk through the attached PDF in a 20-minute call tomorrow.

Thanks again —
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415‑555‑0126

[Attachments: aperture_benchmark_results_v1.csv (CSV, 78KB), load_test_config.yaml (YAML, 2.8KB), aperture_acceptance_summary.pdf (PDF, 110KB)]
